source.title: All Roads Lead to Rome? Exploring Representational Similarities Between Latent Spaces of Generative Image Models
source.authors: Charumathi Badrinath; Usha Bhalla; Alex Oesterling; Suraj Srinivas; Himabindu Lakkaraju

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure values are not available as readable numbers in the text.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether different generative models have similar latent representations using linear latent-space maps, stitching, and probe agreement, rather than the original distance-geometry or seed-comparison methods.
record.gate_note: The paper measures latent-space transfer and probe-prediction agreement. Standalone probe accuracies are not recorded as cross-model alignment results. The ridge-regression α values are tuning settings, not findings. Related-work results cited by the paper are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study fits linear maps between frozen latent spaces of five independently trained generative image models (GAN, VAE, VQVAE, NF, DM) on CelebA. It then measures stitched reconstructions (latent MSE, RMSE, LPIPS, FID) and probe-prediction agreement. This is a direct test of V4's linear-map and stitching interchangeability in a new model family. It does not vary scale, seeds or modality, and it does not test metric dependence.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that stitchability depends on both latent spaces being linearly separable. They offer the idea that more expressive models converge to an 'optimal' representation only as a hypothesis, which they do not test.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired data to fit linear maps between generative-model latent spaces and evaluates stitched reconstructions and attribute-probe agreement. This differs from the Platonic paper's distance-geometry comparisons and from same-architecture seed comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by encoder/model pair and by attribute; gender-related attributes show especially high probe agreement. The paper uses multiple reconstruction and probe-based measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe accuracy on a single Glow NF latent space plateaus by epoch 6 of 26. Reconstructions from partially trained encoders improve only slightly after epoch 11.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearly probeable latent structure in a generative flow model stabilises early in training.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted by the Structured Probabilistic Inference & Generative Modeling workshop of ICML 2024
record.problems: All models are trained on CelebA, and the DM representation is a noised image rather than a conventional learned encoding. Exact figure values and uncertainty estimates are not provided in the text. The study does not test out-of-distribution data or compare alignment against model scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Standalone probe-accuracy results for individual attributes and map-fitting regularization settings are not recorded as cross-model alignment findings.

untested.parts: Model size and capability are not varied. The 'more expressive models converge' statement in the Discussion is a hypothesis, not a result.
No vision–language or paired image–caption comparison.
Untested: relative representations, mapping without paired data, intermediate-layer stitching, and datasets beyond CelebA faces.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit recurrence. Probe agreement on attributes is not unit-level universality.
The study does not vary the similarity measure's settings or test out-of-distribution inputs. It uses only CelebA and CelebA-Synthetic, and its several metrics agree rather than diverge.

No test of plateaus or of shared data or objectives as the cause. The attribute-level explanation (uniform representation or high variance) is a hypothesis only. The VAE and DM failures are attributed to encoder information loss.

missing.what: Probe-match percentages for non-gender attributes, which are lower than for gender attributes (the contrast behind the 'gender most similar' claim)
Reconstructions when other encoders are stitched to the GAN decoder (CelebA-Synthetic), which preserve age, hair, skin and expression
Train vs test MSE of the latent maps (a check on overfitting, given the ridge regularisation on NF and DM maps)

record.verdict_notes: Every row's values are figure-only. The study is not an original source. The reader's V6 and V7 labels rested on variation across encoders and attributes, which is model dependence rather than measure or input dependence, so they were dropped. All models are trained on a single dataset (CelebA).

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of model size or capability against cross-model representational alignment.
No vision-language model comparison or paired image-caption representations.
No independently initialized seeds of the same architecture are compared.
Tests linear maps between generative image-model latent spaces; does not test layer stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
The paper tests attribute-probe agreement, not recurrence of the same neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Compares reconstruction-based and probe-based measures on CelebA, but does not test other datasets, out-of-distribution inputs, or neighbour-count settings.
Reports incomplete transfer for some model pairs, but does not test whether shared data or objectives cause the similarity, or whether cross-model alignment plateaus.

rows.baseline: Random encoder; exact metric values not stated
rows.note: The authors attribute poor VAE transfer partly to information loss during encoding.

rows.subject: Probes on NF, VAE, VQVAE, and GAN latent spaces (aggregate stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compare probe predictions on native and linearly mapped latents

conditions.value: gender-related, particularly Heavy Makeup and Male

rows.value: High for gender-related attributes; exact percentages are figure-only
rows.note: Text says these attributes are represented similarly by nearly every model; it also notes high matches for maps originating from the DM latent space.
rows.check: Holds only for gender-related attributes. The agreement shown is for maps from the GAN latent space (and also from the DM for gender attributes). Attribute-dependence is not V6's similarity-measure or input dependence, so remove V6.

source_check.correct: Probes trained on NF, VAE and VQVAE latents are compared on native latents and latents mapped from GAN. High gender-attribute agreement is also reported for maps originating from DM. GAN is a mapping source, not a probed target.
source_check.problem: The subject incorrectly includes probes trained on the GAN latent space.

rows.subject: NF and VQVAE probes (cross-mapped latent spaces)
rows.operation_detail: Compare probe predictions on each model's latents and latents mapped from the other model
rows.value: NF probes give similar predictions on native and mapped VQVAE latents, and vice versa; exact values are figure-only
rows.note: The text explicitly describes similar predictions in both mapping directions.
rows.check: Remove V6. No attribute is specified and the values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Probes on less linearly separable latent spaces (aggregate stated)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate probes on latents mapped from a more linearly separable space

conditions.value: more linearly separable → less linearly separable latent space

rows.measure: Change in probe accuracy on mapped latents
rows.baseline: Probe accuracy on the model's own latents; exact values not stated
rows.value: Accuracy often increases on mapped latents; exact values are figure-only
rows.note: The authors explain that probes on less linearly separable spaces can be more accurate when applied to mapped latents from a more linearly separable space.
rows.check: A rise in probe accuracy after mapping is not low-loss transfer: the paper defines near-0 change as better. The row shows that mapped latents carry attribute signal, but it cannot show interchangeability.

rows.subject: Glow NF checkpoints
rows.operation_detail: Track linear-probe accuracy on frozen latent spaces during training
rows.value: Accuracy begins to plateau for all attributes by epoch 6 of 26; gender-correlated attributes and Smiling change minimally after epoch 1 of 26
rows.note: This tracks probe accuracy within one model's training, not cross-model alignment or convergence with model scale.
rows.check: Probe accuracy within one model's training; no cross-model measure. The link is correct.

rows.subject: Partially trained Glow NF encoder with fully trained Glow NF decoder
rows.stage_stated: partially trained encoder; fully trained decoder
rows.operation_detail: Reconstruct images using latents from progressively trained NF encoders
rows.value: Quality improves with encoder training; latent space changes minimally after epoch 11
rows.note: This is within-model training progress and does not measure cross-model alignment.
rows.check: Within-model training progress. The link is correct.

relationships.condition: NF and VQVAE encoders linearly stitched to other models' decoders; probe agreement between NF and VQVAE, and on maps from the GAN latent space for gender attributes
relationships.reason: Reconstruction metrics are relatively low for NF and VQVAE encoders to any decoder, and probe predictions match across mapped latents (R1–R8, R11, R12).
relationships.display_finding: NF and VQVAE encoders produced relatively low reconstruction metrics with other decoders, and probe predictions agreed across mapped latent spaces.

relation.reason: The study directly measures whether simple linear maps preserve information between independently trained generative-model representations.

tranche.reason: Linear latent-space stitching, reconstruction metrics and probe agreement test interchangeability through a different method from the original distance-geometry comparison.

source_check.notes: Exact heatmap and probe-match values are unavailable in the supplied text; qualitative results are readable. DM latents are heavily noised images, and DM-decoder reconstructions can preserve geometry while losing colors.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The authors report relatively low reconstruction metrics for NF and VQVAE encoder mappings and similar probe predictions in the NF↔VQVAE mapping (R1–R8, R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: VAE and DM encoders stitched to other decoders
reader_labels.reason: These encoders barely outperform a random encoder in reconstruction quality, so successful linear transfer is not uniform across the tested models (R9–R10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CelebA comparisons using reconstruction and probe-based measures
reader_labels.reason: Transfer varies across encoders, while probe agreement is especially high for gender-related attributes; the reported findings therefore depend on which representation and measure are considered (R1–R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Linear transfer from VAE and DM encoders
reader_labels.reason: The VAE and DM transfer results are weak relative to the random-encoder baseline, showing that the reported similarity is incomplete and model-dependent (R9–R10).
